examples.ko: 저는 그림 그리기를 좋아해서 매일 연습해요.
examples.en: I like drawing, so I practice every day.
In drawing time, I drew my family's faces.
The child likes making things more than drawing.
I'm going to enter a drawing contest this weekend.
Drawing helps calm the mind.
I went to the stationery shop to buy drawing tools.

explain: '그리다'에 '-기'가 붙은 말로, 학교 수업이나 활동 이름에 자주 나와요(그리기 대회, 그리기 시간). 취미를 말할 때는 '그림 그리기'라고 하면 더 자연스러워요. '그림'은 결과물이고 '그리기'는 하는 활동이에요.

phrases.en: Drawing is my hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미나 활동을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to talk about drawing as a hobby or activity.

phrases.en: There is a drawing contest next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 지역 행사 이름에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in names of school or local events.

phrases.en: I packed my drawing supplies in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연필, 물감처럼 그림에 쓰는 물건을 묶어 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group name for things used in drawing, like pencils and paints.

explain_en: Made from '그리다' plus '-기', and common in school or event names (그리기 대회). For a hobby, '그림 그리기' sounds more natural. '그림' is the picture itself; '그리기' is the activity.

examples.en: Disco was hugely popular in the seventies.

examples.ko: 아버지는 젊었을 때 디스코를 자주 추셨대요.
examples.en: I heard my father often danced disco when he was young.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 디스코 리듬이라서 저절로 몸이 움직여요.
examples.en: This song has a disco rhythm, so my body moves on its own.

examples.ko: 신나는 디스코에 맞춰 다 같이 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: We all danced together to the upbeat disco.

examples.ko: 디스코도 좋지만 저는 발라드가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: Disco is nice, but I like ballads more.

examples.ko: 디스코와 팝송이 많이 나오는 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a movie with a lot of disco and pop songs.

explain: 디스코는 음악도 춤도 가리켜요. 춤은 '추다'와 함께 써서 '디스코를 추다'라고 해요. '디스코 음악', '디스코 리듬'처럼 다른 명사 앞에도 붙여요.

phrases.en: I danced disco with friends on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤을 말할 때는 '추다'와 함께 써요. '디스코를 하다'보다 '추다'가 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: When it means the dance, use it with '추다'; it sounds more natural than '하다'.

phrases.en: Disco music plays in this shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '음악'을 붙이면 춤이 아니라 음악이라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '음악' makes it clear you mean the music, not the dance.

phrases.en: My grandmother showed me a disco dance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '춤'을 붙이면 음악이 아니라 춤이라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '춤' makes it clear you mean the dance, not the music.

explain_en: 디스코 can mean both the music and the dance. For the dance it pairs with '추다', as in '디스코를 추다'. It also goes before other nouns, like '디스코 음악' and '디스코 리듬'.

examples.en: This team's mascot is a tiger.
The mascot danced in the stadium.
The children took photos with the mascot.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 마스코트를 새로 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: We are creating a new mascot for our school.
I attached a small mascot doll to my bag.
The Olympic mascot will be announced soon too.

explain: 팀, 학교, 행사를 대표하는 캐릭터예요. 동물 모양이 많고, '마스코트 인형'처럼 물건으로도 만들어 팔아요.

phrases.en: I got a mascot doll as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마스코트를 인형으로 만든 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mascot made into a doll.

phrases.en: Our team's mascot is a bear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀을 대표하는 캐릭터를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the character that represents a team.

phrases.en: The mascot character is really cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 모양으로 된 대표 캐릭터를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the representative character as a design.

explain_en: It is the character that represents a team, school, or event. Many are animals, and they are also made into goods, like a 마스코트 인형.

examples.en: The groom and bride stood facing each other and bowed in return.
The two of them greeted each other with a mutual bow.
How should we do the mutual bow at the wedding?

examples.ko: 스승과 제자가 서로 맞절하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was lovely to see the teacher and student bowing to each other.
Before bowing to each other, I first straightened my clothes.

examples.ko: 사회자가 신랑 신부에게 이제 맞절하라고 말했어요.
examples.en: The MC told the bride and groom to bow to each other now.

explain: '절하다'와 달리 두 사람이 서로 같이 절을 주고받을 때 써요. 한 사람만 절을 올리면 '절하다'나 '절을 올리다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 두 사람이 서로 맞절하고 자리에 앉았어요.
phrases.en: The two bowed to each other and sat down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 붙이면 둘이 함께 절을 주고받는다는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'seoro' makes it clearer that both bow to each other.

phrases.en: After bowing to each other, they started eating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞절이 끝난 뒤에 이어지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what happens after the mutual bow.

phrases.en: Please face each other and bow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예식에서 순서를 안내할 때 쓰는 높임 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite imperative used to guide people through a ceremony.

explain_en: Unlike '절하다', it is used when two people bow to each other. If only one person bows, you say '절하다' or '절을 올리다'.

examples.ko: 맨몸으로 할 수 있는 운동을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me exercises I can do without equipment.

examples.ko: 그는 가방도 없이 맨몸으로 집을 나왔어요.
examples.en: He left the house empty-handed, without even a bag.

examples.ko: 맨몸 운동은 헬스장에 가지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: Bodyweight exercise doesn't require going to a gym.

examples.ko: 불이 나서 맨몸으로 겨우 도망쳐 나왔대요.
examples.en: I heard there was a fire and they barely escaped with nothing.

examples.ko: 맨몸으로 시작해서 지금은 가게가 두 개예요.
examples.en: I started with nothing, and now I have two shops.
Going out with nothing in hand, without a bag, feels light.

explain: 일상에서는 옷을 벗은 몸보다 도구나 재산 없이 몸 하나뿐인 상태를 말할 때 많이 써요. '맨몸 운동'은 기구 없이 자기 몸무게로 하는 운동이에요. 옷을 안 입은 몸은 보통 '알몸'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I do bodyweight exercises at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기구 없이 자기 몸무게로 하는 운동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Exercise using only your own body weight, without equipment.

phrases.example: 그는 맨몸으로 서울에 와서 일을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: He came to Seoul empty-handed and started working.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 재산 없이 처음부터 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting from scratch with no money or belongings.

phrases.en: The baby bathes naked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 안 입은 몸은 '맨몸'보다 '알몸'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a body without clothes, 'almom' is used instead of 'maenmom'.

explain_en: In daily speech it is used more for having only your own body, with no tools or money, than for being unclothed. '맨몸 운동' is exercise done with your own body weight and no equipment. For a body without clothes, people usually say '알몸'.

examples.en: The child leans on the wall and practices handstands.
You need arm strength to do a handstand.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 물구나무서기를 하고 걸을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling can even walk while doing a handstand.
Handstands were hard, so I kept falling over.
We bet on who could hold a handstand the longest.

examples.ko: 물구나무서기 자세로 십 초만 버텨 보세요.
examples.en: Try holding the handstand position for just ten seconds.

explain: 손으로 바닥을 짚고 거꾸로 서는 동작이에요. 동사로는 '물구나무서다'나 '물구나무를 서다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I can do a handstand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '물구나무서기'의 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of the noun 물구나무서기.

phrases.en: I practice handstands against the wall every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작을 배우거나 연습할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when learning or practicing the movement.

phrases.en: We did a handstand in yoga class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 동작을 한다는 뜻으로 '하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 하다 to mean doing the exercise or movement.

explain_en: It is the move of standing upside down on your hands. As a verb you can say '물구나무서다' or '물구나무를 서다'.

examples.en: That player's footwork is really fast.
Footwork is important when you dance.

examples.ko: 권투 선수는 발놀림 하나로 상대를 피했어요.
examples.en: The boxer dodged his opponent with footwork alone.
My footwork is clumsy, so my steps keep getting tangled.

examples.ko: 축구 감독이 어린 선수의 발놀림을 칭찬했어요.
examples.en: The soccer coach praised the young player's footwork.

examples.ko: 가벼운 발놀림에 맞춰 음악이 점점 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: The music got faster to match the light footwork.

explain: 스포츠나 춤에서 발을 움직이는 솜씨를 말할 때 써요. '손놀림', '몸놀림'처럼 몸의 부분 뒤에 '-놀림'을 붙인 짝말이 있고, 같은 뜻으로 '풋워크'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: That dancer has light footwork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발을 움직이는 솜씨가 부드럽고 빠르다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the way someone moves their feet is smooth and quick.

phrases.en: He dodged the opponent with quick footwork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서 발을 재빨리 움직일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for moving the feet quickly in sports.

phrases.en: Footwork is important in boxing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발놀림'과 같은 뜻의 외래어로, 스포츠에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword with the same meaning as 발놀림, often heard in sports.

explain_en: It is used for how skillfully someone moves their feet in sports or dance. It has sibling words like '손놀림' and '몸놀림', and people also say '풋워크' for the same thing.

examples.en: Kicking is important when you swim.
I practice kicks in taekwondo.

examples.ko: 아이가 힘껏 발차기를 해서 공을 멀리 보냈어요.
examples.en: The child gave a hard kick and sent the ball far away.
Kicking takes a lot of leg strength.
The opponent fell down with a single kick.
My legs hurt from kick practice.

explain: 발로 차는 동작을 말하며, 태권도와 수영에서 가장 자주 들려요. 수영에서는 '킥'이라고도 하고, 말할 때는 '발차기를 하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I do a hundred kicks every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발로 차는 동작을 할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for doing the motion of kicking.

phrases.en: My legs hurt when I practice kicking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 배울 때 연습한다는 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when practicing kicks in a sport.

phrases.en: In swimming, a kick is also called a 'kick'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영어에서 온 말이에요. 수영장에서 '발차기' 대신 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word from English, often used at the pool instead of 'bal-chagi'.

explain_en: It is the kicking motion, heard most often in taekwondo and swimming. In swimming people also say 킥, and the common phrase is '발차기를 하다'.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 같은 멜로디의 변주가 계속 나와요.
examples.en: In this piece, variations of the same melody keep appearing.
I'm practicing an easy variation on the piano.
This movie is a modern variation on an old tale.

examples.ko: 요리사가 전통 음식에 작은 변주를 줬어요.
examples.en: The chef added a small twist to the traditional dish.
Even the same song is varied differently by each singer.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 신데렐라 이야기의 변주 같아요.
examples.en: This drama seems like a variation on the Cinderella story.

explain: 원래는 음악에서 같은 주제를 바꿔 가며 되풀이하는 것을 가리켜요. 일상에서는 기본 틀은 두고 조금 바꾼 것을 말할 때 비유로 써요. '변형'보다 예술적인 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: This set of variations is very famous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 주제를 바꿔 가며 만든 곡을 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for a piece built on variations of one theme.

phrases.en: I vary the same theme little by little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변주'를 동사로 쓴 꼴이고, 음악뿐 아니라 이야기나 요리에도 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, also used figuratively for stories or cooking.

phrases.en: I changed the basic design a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변주'보다 예술 느낌이 약하고 모양이나 틀이 바뀐 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less artistic than '변주'; it just means a changed form.

explain_en: Originally a music term for repeating one theme with changes. In daily speech it is used figuratively for something that keeps a basic frame but is altered a little. It feels more artistic than '변형'.

examples.en: I play the viola in the orchestra.
The viola is a bit bigger than the violin.

examples.ko: 동생은 비올라 수업을 받은 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has taken viola lessons for a year.
The viola sounds lower and warmer than the violin.
We are short one viola player.
In this piece, the viola carries the melody.

explain: 바이올린보다 크고 첼로보다 작아서 소리 높이도 그 사이예요. 연주할 때는 '연주하다'가 가장 무난하고, 바이올린처럼 '켜다'도 쓸 수 있어요. 오케스트라 이야기에서 바이올린, 첼로와 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling plays the viola at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연주하다'보다 악기를 활로 켠다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 'play (연주하다)', it stresses drawing the bow across the strings.

phrases.en: That person is a famous viola player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비올라를 연주하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It names the person who plays the viola.

phrases.en: The sound of the viola is soft and warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about how the instrument sounds.

explain_en: It is bigger than the violin and smaller than the cello, so its pitch sits between them. '연주하다' is the safest verb, and '켜다' works as with the violin. It often appears with the violin and cello in orchestra talk.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 골대 앞에서 열심히 수비했어요.
examples.en: Our team defended hard in front of the goal.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 상대 에이스를 수비하는 역할이에요.
examples.en: That player's role is to defend against the opposing ace.

examples.ko: 공격할 때보다 수비할 때가 더 힘들어요.
examples.en: Defending is harder than attacking.

examples.ko: 끝까지 수비하고 나서 마지막에 점수를 냈어요.
examples.en: They held the defense until the end and then scored late.
This time they pulled back in order to defend.
We talked with the coach about how we should defend.

explain: 경기에서 점수를 막는 일은 '수비', 점수를 내는 일은 '공격'이에요. 경기 밖에서 물건이나 사람을 지킬 때는 '지키다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Our team has a strong defense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '수비'를 써서 팀의 힘을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 수비 to describe a team's strength.

phrases.en: The goalkeeper stopped the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이에요. 점수를 못 내게 할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word, also used for stopping the other side from scoring.

phrases.en: In soccer, I'm a defender.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수비하는 선수를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a player who defends.

explain_en: In a game, stopping the other side from scoring is '수비' and scoring is '공격'. Outside of sports, when you protect an object or a person, use '지키다'.

dis.h: play defense, esp. in sports or war

p.n: 방어 is more general and works outside sports too.

examples.en: The ball flew high toward the outfield.
Our team's outfield defense is weak.
I cheered with my friends in the outfield seats.

examples.ko: 타자가 친 공이 외야를 가르고 굴러갔어요.
examples.en: The ball the batter hit split the outfield and rolled away.
When the fly ball went to the outfield, the runner ran.

examples.ko: 야구장에서 외야 자리가 싸서 거기서 봤어요.
examples.en: Outfield seats at the ballpark were cheap, so I watched from there.

explain: 야구에서 내야의 바깥쪽 넓은 부분이고, 반대말은 '내야'예요. 외야를 지키는 선수는 좌익수, 중견수, 우익수이고, 외야 쪽 관중석은 '외야석'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 외야석에서 보면 경기장이 아주 넓어 보여요.
phrases.en: From the outfield seats, the stadium looks very wide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외야 쪽에 있는 관중석을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spectator seats on the outfield side.

phrases.en: The batter hit the ball toward the outfield.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공이 가는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell the direction the ball goes.

phrases.en: The ball dropped between the infield and the outfield.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '내야'와 함께 써서 야구장의 안쪽과 바깥쪽을 나눠요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with its opposite 'naeya' to split the inner and outer field.

explain_en: In baseball, it is the wide area beyond the infield, and the opposite is '내야'. The players who guard it are the left fielder, center fielder and right fielder, and the seats there are called '외야석'.

examples.en: A fairy came out of the magic lamp.
My daughter wants a magic wand.
Like magic, the room became clean in an instant.

examples.ko: 이 그림책에는 요술을 부리는 고양이가 나와요.
examples.en: This picture book has a cat that does magic.

examples.ko: 요술 거울을 보면 미래가 보인다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you can see the future in the magic mirror.
I read a fairy tale about a grandmother who works magic.

explain: '마술'은 손기술로 보여 주는 쇼를 떠올리게 하고, '요술'은 동화처럼 신기한 힘으로 일이 일어나는 느낌이에요. '요술 램프', '요술 지팡이'처럼 이야기 속 물건에 잘 붙어요. '요술을 부리다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The child plays, waving a magic wand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화 속 마법의 지팡이를 가리켜요. 아이들의 장난감 이름으로도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A magic wand from fairy tales; also a common name for children's toys.

phrases.example: 요정이 요술을 부려서 호박이 마차가 됐어요.
phrases.en: The fairy used magic and the pumpkin became a carriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요술'과 가장 잘 어울리는 동사예요. 이야기 속에서 신기한 일이 일어날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that pairs best with 요술, used when something wondrous happens in a story.

phrases.en: In the fairy tale, the queen asked the magic mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화에 나오는 신기한 거울이에요. 요술 뒤에 이야기 속 물건 이름을 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A wondrous mirror from fairy tales; you can attach story objects after 요술.

explain_en: 마술 usually brings to mind a stage show of sleight of hand, while 요술 has a fairy-tale feel of mysterious power at work. It attaches well to storybook items like 요술 램프 and 요술 지팡이. The verb pattern is '요술을 부리다' (to work magic).

examples.en: The children watched the puppet show and laughed loudly.
A puppet show is held at the library on weekends.
I prepared a puppet show at the daycare.
The rabbit in the puppet show was really cute.
Babies love hand-operated puppet shows.

examples.ko: 공원에서 열린 인형극 덕분에 하루가 즐거웠어요.
examples.en: The puppet show in the park made the day fun.

explain: 인형을 움직여서 이야기를 보여 주는 공연이에요. 사람이 나오는 연극은 그냥 '연극'이라고 해요. 아이들 행사나 도서관 프로그램에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: On the weekend I go to see a puppet show with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연을 보러 갈 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say you are going to see a show.
phrases.en_equiv: to go see a puppet show

phrases.en: There is a puppet show performance in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사 안내에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in event announcements.

phrases.en: I did a play with my friends at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 나와서 하는 공연은 '인형극'이 아니라 '연극'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A show with real people acting is 연극, not 인형극.

explain_en: 인형극 is a performance where puppets act out a story. A play with human actors is just 연극. You often find it at children's events and library programs.

en: to make a lyric; to write a lyric

examples.en: My friend wrote the lyrics of this song.
I wrote the lyrics myself and sang it.
That singer wrote both lyrics and music herself.
I like writing lyrics as a hobby.
Do you know who wrote the lyrics of this song?
When writing lyrics, I also think about the rhythm of words.

explain: 노래 가사를 쓰는 일이고, 곡을 만드는 일은 '작곡하다'예요. 둘이 짝이라 '작사·작곡'으로 같이 쓰고, 노래 정보에도 이름이 따로 적혀 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 작사가는 유명한 노래를 많이 썼어요.
phrases.en: That lyricist wrote many famous songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작사하는 사람을 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for a person who writes lyrics.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 작사·작곡을 모두 가수가 했어요.
phrases.en: The singer did both the lyrics and the music for this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가사와 곡을 짝으로 묶어 노래 정보를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs lyrics and composition when giving song credits.

phrases.en: I wrote song lyrics for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작사하다'보다 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase than 작사하다, common in daily talk.

explain_en: It means writing the words of a song, while composing the music is '작곡하다'. The two are a pair, written together as '작사·작곡', and song credits list each name separately.

examples.en: On Seollal we play jegichagi with the family.
How many kicks have you managed in jegichagi?

examples.ko: 제기차기 대회에서 우리 반이 일등 했어요.
examples.en: Our class won first place in the jegichagi contest.

examples.ko: 제기차기도 해 보고 윷놀이도 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried jegichagi and yutnori too.

examples.ko: 제기차기에 도전했는데 한 번도 못 찼어요.
examples.en: I tried jegichagi but could not kick it even once.
Kite flying, jegichagi and neolttwigi are Korean folk games.

explain: 놀이에 쓰는 물건 이름이 '제기'라서 '제기를 차다'라고도 말해요. 제사 때 쓰는 그릇인 '제기(祭器)'와 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요. 설날 무렵 윷놀이, 연날리기 같은 민속놀이와 함께 많이 이야기해요.

phrases.en: The children are kicking the jegi in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제기차기'를 놀이 이름이 아니라 행동으로 풀어 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes the action instead of using the game's name.

phrases.en: A jegichagi contest was held at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이로 겨루는 행사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for an event where people compete at the game.

phrases.en: My grandfather is very good at jegichagi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the easiest phrase for talking about skill.

explain_en: The object used in the game is called a '제기', so you can also say '제기를 차다'. It sounds the same as '제기(祭器)', the vessels used for ancestral rites, but it is a different word. People often talk about it around Seollal together with folk games like yutnori and kite flying.

examples.en: He carves faces out of stone.
My grandfather carved a bird out of wood.
I watched the carving up close.
They carved ice to make a decoration.
The carved work is in the museum.
If you carve soap, it becomes a pretty flower.

explain: '조각'은 케이크 한 조각의 '조각'과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이에요. 예술의 '조각'은 '조각가'가 나무나 돌을 깎는 일이에요. 글자나 무늬를 파서 남기는 일은 '새기다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father carved a doll out of wood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조각하다' 앞에 재료를 넣어 무엇을 깎는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the material before the verb to say what is being carved.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 지금 큰 돌을 조각하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That person is carving a big stone right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조각하는 일이 지금 진행 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the carving is happening right now.

phrases.en: The work my grandfather carved is in the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조각하다'를 '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes a noun, like a work that someone carved.

explain_en: '조각' also means a piece, as in a piece of cake, but that is a different word with the same sound. The art word '조각' is what a '조각가' (sculptor) does with wood or stone. '새기다' is a related word for engraving.

examples.en: I practiced with a friend at the table tennis table.

examples.ko: 학교 체육관에 탁구대가 네 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are four table tennis tables in the school gym.
I folded the table tennis table and stood it against the wall.
I'm looking into buying a new table tennis table.
The ball fell on the table tennis table.
Shall we play a game at our table?

explain: 탁구를 치는 '대(판)'를 말하고, 탁구를 하는 장소는 '탁구장'이라고 해서 구별해요. 보통 '탁구를 치다'라고 말해요. 가운데 있는 그물은 '네트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The ball fell onto the table-tennis table.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위'와 함께 써서 탁구대의 판 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '위' to mean the playing surface.

phrases.en: We set up a new ping-pong table in the gym.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁구대를 설치하거나 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting up or placing a table.
phrases.en_equiv: to set up a ping-pong table

phrases.en: There is a net in the middle of the ping-pong table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁구대의 부품을 말할 때 이렇게 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a part belonging to the table.

explain_en: This is the table itself, while the place for playing is called '탁구장', so keep them apart. People normally say '탁구를 치다'. The net in the middle is called '네트'.

examples.en: At karaoke, my friend shook the tambourine.
The kindergarten kids sang while hitting tambourines.

examples.ko: 탬버린 소리가 신나서 저절로 박수가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The tambourine sound was so lively that I started clapping.
I took charge of the tambourine in the band.

examples.ko: 탬버린은 박자에 맞춰 치면 훨씬 재미있어요.
examples.en: A tambourine is much more fun when you hit it in time with the beat.
An old tambourine turned up in the drawer.

explain: '탬버린'은 한국에서 노래방에 꼭 있는 도구라서 악기보다 '분위기를 띄우는 물건'으로 더 많이 알려졌어요. '탬버린을 치다', '탬버린을 흔들다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: We clapped along with the sound of the tambourine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기가 내는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the sound the instrument makes.

phrases.en: I danced holding a tambourine at karaoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 들고 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe holding it in your hand.

phrases.en: We played the tambourine in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기로 쓴다는 뜻이라서 음악 수업 이야기에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Treats it as an instrument, fitting for music class.

explain_en: '탬버린' is found in almost every Korean karaoke room, so it is known more as a party-livening prop than as an instrument. People say '탬버린을 치다' or '탬버린을 흔들다'.

examples.ko: 저는 턱걸이를 열 개 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do ten chin-ups.
I did chin-ups on the bar in the park.
Chin-ups are good exercise for the arms and back.

examples.ko: 턱걸이가 너무 어려워서 한 개도 못 해요.
examples.en: Chin-ups are so hard that I can't do even one.
I'm practicing chin-ups a little every day.
My shoulder hurt while I was doing chin-ups.

explain: 철봉을 잡고 몸을 끌어올려 턱이 철봉 위로 오게 하는 운동이에요. 바닥에서 하는 '팔굽혀펴기'와 구별해요. 보통 '턱걸이를 하다'라고 말해요. 아래처럼 겨우 해냈다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: My score was borderline, but I just barely passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준에 겨우 맞춰 간신히 통과한다는 뜻이에요. 시험, 입학, 심사 같은 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means just barely meeting the cutoff. Used for exams, admissions and screenings.

explain_en: It is the exercise of pulling yourself up on a bar until your chin is over it. Do not mix it up with '팔굽혀펴기' (push-ups), done on the floor. It is normally said as '턱걸이를 하다'. It is also used to mean barely managing something, as shown below.

examples.en: My older brother is learning hapkido.
At the hapkido dojang we practiced how to fall first.
Hapkido is a sport that uses the opponent's force.
I went to the gym to see a hapkido demonstration.
I go to hapkido class every weekend.
How are hapkido and taekwondo different?

explain: 한국에는 태권도, 합기도, 검도, 유도처럼 '-도'로 끝나는 무술 이름이 많아요. 합기도는 상대를 잡고 던지는 기술이 많아서 발차기가 중심인 태권도와 느낌이 달라요. '합기도를 하다/배우다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I have done hapkido since I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배우다'보다 오래 운동해 왔다는 느낌으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 배우다, it can suggest practicing for a long time.

phrases.en: The hapkido master corrected my posture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무술을 가르치는 선생님을 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for a martial arts instructor.

phrases.en: There is a hapkido class every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 시간이나 수업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about class times.

explain_en: Many Korean martial arts end in '-도', such as 태권도, 합기도, 검도 and 유도. Hapkido has many grabbing and throwing techniques, so it feels different from taekwondo, which centers on kicks. You say '합기도를 하다/배우다'.

examples.ko: 아빠가 설거지를 하면서 노래를 흥얼흥얼 불러요.
examples.en: Dad hums a song while doing the dishes.

examples.ko: 길을 걷다가 저도 모르게 흥얼흥얼 따라 불렀어요.
examples.en: While walking, I found myself humming along without realizing it.
He cleaned his room, humming a tune.
I could hear someone humming while they showered.

examples.ko: 어머니가 흥얼흥얼 옛 노래를 부르며 요리하세요.
examples.en: My mother cooks while humming an old song.

examples.ko: 운전하면서 라디오 노래를 흥얼흥얼 따라 했어요.
examples.en: I hummed along to the radio while driving.

explain: 기분이 좋거나 무심코 작은 소리로 노래를 부르는 모습이에요. 보통 '노래를 흥얼흥얼 부르다'처럼 쓰고, 동사로는 '흥얼거리다'를 더 많이 말해요. 크게 노래하는 것이 아니라 혼자 중얼거리듯 부르는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I hum a song while showering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흥얼흥얼'의 동사형으로 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '흥얼흥얼', used more in daily speech.

phrases.en: He must be in a good mood, humming a tune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋을 때 혼자 작게 부르는 콧노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quiet humming that one does alone when in a good mood.

phrases.en: I hummed along to the commercial jingle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 노래를 작은 소리로 따라 부르는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quietly following along with a song you heard.

explain_en: It describes softly singing to yourself, usually when you are in a good mood or without thinking. It is typically used as in '노래를 흥얼흥얼 부르다', and as a verb people more often say '흥얼거리다'. It is not full-voiced singing but more like singing under your breath.
